notes.title: Update
notes.notes:
You have known these stories since childhood. Now it’s time to survive their darker side.





[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/4b0330b1b3eaf1c56ba543746dd3654bc77de13a.png"]

Once upon a time, there was a maiden of such grace and gentleness that the people of the kingdom called her Snow White. Her lips were red as roses, her hair dark as ebony, her skin pale as fallen snow. Wherever she passed, even the mirrors of her father’s castle seemed to glow.



But the blessing of beauty weighed on her like a chain. No one saw Sophia, the princess and heiress—they saw only Snow White, a vision to be admired, a name spoken with sighs until her true self was lost. Her bright eyes dulled, her thoughts drifted like mist, and she wandered farther from the castle walls with each passing day. Only a pocket-glass kept her company.

Then came famine. The fields withered, the treasury emptied, and the people’s faces grew hollow. Snow White strayed beyond the walls, into the old coal mines, deserted even by the dwarves who once dug there. Save for one, too weary to depart and too stubborn to perish.



In those black tunnels she lingered, feeding on bitter red apples touched by plague, speaking only to the coughing dwarf and her faithful mirror. No prince came riding to her rescue. Only the Rat King, cast out of the capital, his crown broken, his claws keener than his heart. He found her there, pale as cerement, and spoke a bargain: together they should take the throne, not in wedlock, but in crime.



Snow White, silent and hollow-eyed, did not gainsay him. The Rat King set her mirror upon a revolver by craft of alchemy and steel, and thereby claimed her trust. With the old dwarf at their side and baskets of poisoned fruit in their hands, they set their steps toward the castle. And Snow White’s gaze, hollow for many years, shone once more.



The lesson of this tale? Perhaps there is none. But within it lie treasures, and not all of them are make-believe:



- Snow White—a princess of sorrowful beauty, now with a tale twisted anew. A happy ending? Such things are seldom told.

- The Rat King—a proud outcast, crownless and cast aside. His own throne was lost, yet he made certain the Nutcracker’s fell as well.

- Deadly Reflection—a revolver wrought with Snow White’s pocket-glass. She had gazed into it so long that now each shot carries her charms, lulling prey into stillness before the venom takes them.

- Death’s Fruit — the plague given flesh in the shape of sacred apples. Whoever tastes them is slowed, poisoned, and drained of life. And the old dwarf tends the harvest still, for this has become his grim calling.




[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/87f70c8872327f3e302cb4a1af2dc63749ca0b4f.png"]



Do not close the book too soon, for two more tales are yet to be told.



The first speaks of a mermaid, young and curious, who longed for the world of men. She swam near their ships, listened to their fisherman’s songs, watched their strange rituals with shining eyes. Yet the sea is fickle, and human hearts are crueller still.

One night she was spied by sailors, who cast their hooks and hurled their harpoons. They dragged her aboard, pierced her with iron, and nearly split her open. Yet she slipped away, wounded and silent, and sank to the ocean floor. There her love for mankind drowned, and in its place grew only vengeance — small at first, like a hatchling, but swelling until it filled her like a great white shark.

Time passed. Ships vanished. Some whispered of the Leviathan, a monster of the deep. But the oldest sea-wolves knew: there are no monsters in this world, save those men make for themselves.

The second tale tells of a girl in a red cap who went to her grandmother’s house. She carried cakes and pies in her basket and sang merry songs as she walked. Days went by, yet she did not return.

The wolves had grown bold, circling the village, their snarls reaching even the gates. None dared go searching. Then, as swiftly as they had appeared, the wolves were gone. The villagers lit their torches and shouldered their pitchforks, marching to the grandmother’s house.

Halfway there they met her — Little Red Riding Hood. But she was changed. Though only days had passed, she stood taller, her shoulders broad, her waist ringed with gnashing fangs. Crimson stained her face, and in her gentle hands she carried a hatchet, steady and sure. She smiled still, and sang her whimsical song.



And what do these tales bestow upon us? Well, let’s see:

- Little Mermaid—no longer the helpless child of sorrow, but a bearer of vengeance. And note this: she is only the second avatar without feet—for she never bartered away her tail.

- Leviathan Fang—a heavy harpoon, pulling its wielder towards the foe. Few survive its strike; those who do are left bleeding, and do not linger long.

- Little Red Riding Hood—once a merry girl, now a hardened hunter. She loved her grandmother, and loathed the wolves. Should you meet her on the battlefield, it is you who will need the saving.

- Crimson Treat—a three-barrel shotgun, whose song heals its wielder and lays low all who dare oppose it.

- Red Reaper—a powerful axe and a lantern that burns brighter when foes draw near. Together they are a fell pair.

- Silent Howl—a rifle cloaked in wolfskin. To its master it grants armor and strikes most critical. For with each shot, revenge grows sweeter still.





[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/51466ad8f24d2cc45145b456ec522d4e8315478a.png"]



Time to take a break from scary fairytales—the Final Summer Parties are rolling on, and jam #2 is here: Beach Chorus!

What’s it like? Picture sunshine, waves, and sandcastles… sounds a bit too idyllic for Pixel Gun 3D, right? Don’t worry—we’ve spiced it up with a little chaos. Your job is to smash those sandcastles and scoop up rewards: guns, bonuses, Pixelpon tags, plus a one-of-a-kind avatar and ride (they look deliciously good).

To wreck those sandcastles, you’ll need shovels—yep, the small, bright plastic ones you remember from childhood. And there’s only one place to earn them: the battlefield.

F2P-players are getting all the unique prizes plus a chest with a gun. VIP players’ loot list stacked a bit higher: more chests, more guns, more bonuses… and even their own private beach.



So grab a shovel, hit the sand, and let’s make sure everyone leaves this party loaded and happy!





[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/a837732977e4cf63c98f7efafede12627eb5d9a1.png"]

Here it comes—the final power chord of the Final Summer Parties!



The name says it all: you’re invited to the backyard party. But first, you’ll need to rebuild the map to find your way. Need a hint on what to watch for?



Party Booster—a brand-new, shiny yellow gadget that turns you into a giant, party-hard duck armed with Twin Soakers water blasters. It’s kinda like Robot Samurai or Battle Mech—but with even more punch.



Twin Soakers—a backup with piercing shots that slow and mark your target. Fast, mobile, solid damage, and pure party vibes you can bring to any arena.

And don’t forget: the Backyard Reprise activates the Pixelpon event! Tags from the Final Summer Parties give you a shot at the best gear in the game—even the legendary Ultimatum itself.



All of this—to make sure we close out summer with a bang!

notes.notes:
Chrome, gasoline, and pixels—everything burns in Iron Wastelands. Everything. 




[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/45010889e664fdfe5b3d9eea1497e6635017585c.png"]

The clash with Eddie Mesmer in the L-52 facility didn’t bring closure. Instead, it triggered Track_0, a hidden protocol that scattered the Endless Sand across multiple worlds



Mesmer slipped away again, vanishing through a portal. With no time to plan, Pixel Man, Daisy, and the Human Rebel followed—straight into a place no one had mapped: the Iron Wastelands. A scorched nowhere of rusted metal, desert heat, and a two-lane blacktop stretching into infinity.



At the center of it all: The Furnaceborn. His followers call him the Flamefather or the Ember Regent, a fanatic with a vision—bending time and matter into one fused machine at his legendary Time Forge. “Burn or be burned!” is his law. These words still cling to rust-bitten signs, half-buried in ash. Turns out, Furnaceborn used to serve Mesmer. Not anymore: now he’s focused on his own plan—and Mesmer’s in the way. The Furnaceborn wants the hypnotist gone.



That might sound like luck, but here’s the catch: Furnaceborn thinks our heroes are a threat too. While he mobilizes his patrols, Pixel Man and the others have to stay ahead—find Mesmer, recover the Endless Sand, and keep it out of the wrong hands. Because if Furnaceborn gets it first, reshaping the Wastelands might be the least of our problems. He’s got the forge. He’s got the will. And he just might have enough insanity to collapse the entire Pixel Universe.



Watch out for:



Elian The Guder—sharp-eyed navigator, ruthless scout, and trigger-happy menace. A genius behind the wheel and a total maniac in the head.



Dusty Rover—V8 engine, twin flame-spitters, roll cage, and armor plate slabs. This ain’t a ride—it’s a runaway freight train on third gear, built to bulldoze through purgatory.



Blazefanner—a mangled, metal-backed freakshow of a weapon. Slows you down, lights you up, and fries anything big enough to twitch inside its scope. Brutal doesn’t begin to cover it.



Technician Greer—if it shoots, burns, or explodes, Greer probably made it. Even the Time Forge itself was cooked up in that cracked head of his. He’s not a technician—he’s a walking war lab.



Prototype Chainsaw Rifle—Greer’s love letter to chaos. A sniper rifle that shoots high-voltage bolts. Comes with X-ray vision and chain damage so nasty, even the Wastelands flinch when it hums.





[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/5125c1eaf3952b0100da799dd0fc51f1d16d7ffc.png"]

More heat from the Wastelands!



Drazz—the wildcard in Furnaceborn’s inner circle. Ragebringer? Strategist? Court jester? Nobody’s sure—not even Drazz. But one thing’s clear: this twisted freak is as unstable as a blast fuse on a short timer. Approach with caution—or better yet, don’t.



Tremor Vox—Drazz’s favorite sidearm. A pistol with a pulse, it feeds on precision. Every headshot amps its damage, making it more unhinged with every pull of the trigger. They call this attribute Headshot Rage. You’ll see why.



The Furnaceborn—the Flamefather himself. Ruler of the Iron Wastelands. Half prophet, half war machine. Avoid at all costs: this guy isn’t particularly famous for taking prisoners.



Rebar Sling—Furnaceborn’s go-to when subtlety isn’t even on the table. A brutal slingshot that fires hunks of scrap and rebar. Fast, ricocheting, and known for nasty gashing wounds.



Rusty Reaper—a long-range rifle fueled by a volatile core. Comes loaded with X-ray Vision, so you’re never really hidden.



Scorching Mauler—the final word in firepower. The Furnaceborn’s personal flame canon. This isn’t a flamethrower—it’s a walking inferno. Slow, heavy, devastating—and beyond anything words can handle.






[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/5b6333c61bfa953b167941bcc93a5893ef911cbc.png"]

In the post-apocalypse, might makes right—but that doesn’t mean you can’t show off some style while you’re at it. And during Emberfest, you’ve got two ways to blaze your trail.



Got spare currency? Hit the in-game shop, grab whatever you want, and earn Festival Coupons as cashback. Stack enough, and you can trade 'em for all kinds of loot—including the headline prize: the ruthless Ember Gut melee weapon.


Low on funds, high on fire? No problem. Dominate in matches to earn Pyroids and swap them for rewards—plus a one-of-a-kind avatar to prove you burned your way through.




[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/2b75eb41bff034d126ccc279321589cb36887cfa.png"]


We’ve crossed summer’s midpoint. Autumn’s creeping in with cooler moods and slower moves—but not yet. There’s still time to go loud. To party like it’s doomsday’s eve.That’s where the Final Summer Parties come in! Three linked events with top-tier rewards. Three parties you can’t miss. Three chances to turn what’s left of summer into a mixtape to remember.






[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/0d31f427127c4c0d2b01cc3ed7180aa6f4b7db03.png"]

The first beat in the Final Summer Parties mixtape. Here's how the rhythm flows:



- Step into the lift 

- Let your skill do the climbing. Floor by floor, frag by frag

- Claim your rewards

- Then hit the rooftop—where the view hits back

A sweet, old-school capsule machine loaded with prizes every pixelgunner wants. You get the hint, right? 



You’ll see it in the lobby—but you won’t get access. Not yet. Pixelpon unlocks toward the end of the Final Summer Parties. The better you perform in the event series, the more precious capsules you’ll earn. Just to make sure summer ends with a BANG. So don’t sit on your hands during the event series.

Gear up smart. Go tactical. Initiate Echo Protocol. Survive the op—if you can.




[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/91a5b0086d0be737b20341116b39ed186a67ab81.png"]


L-52. Most in the Pixel Universe haven’t even heard the name.


A few brilliant minds across different worlds once ran the numbers and came up with a wild theory: somewhere out there, time could be controlled. They never reached it, but the idea was too tempting to ignore. Eventually, a few military groups got involved. Funded off-books and buried deep in \[classified] forest, they built an L-52 facility in \[classified]—a zone where secret experiments were run to bend and sync timelines using satellites and signal relays. No oversight. No ethics. Just decades of unchecked research. And progress—scary progress.


Then, one day, it all stopped.


The barracks, the labs, the relays—they’re still there. Still powered. But the soldiers, scientists, and support crews are long gone. Only unfinished experiments remain—silent, dangerous, and waiting like crocodiles for anyone reckless enough to get close.


After breaking free of Mesmer’s control, Ramlisa used the Timeless Sands to open a portal. Now our heroes are here. L-52. The problem is, Eddie Mesmer got here first. And even the pixel gods don’t know what’s going on in that twisted head of his. Pixel Man, Daisy, and the Human Rebel have to track him down. Fast.


And Mesmer’s not the only thing waiting in this place. L-52 may be forgotten, but it’s still very much alive.



Captain Sower—possibly on an official military op. But no one knows for sure.

He’s armed with the Dustpiercer DMR—a fast, mobile sniper rifle enhanced with Target Mark and a bleeding effect. Efficient. Precise. Cold.

Ironside—once part of Sower’s squad. Scratch that—he is the squad. A soldier through and through, Ironside sees only targets. Anything in his path—irrelevant.

His weapon of choice: the VX-9 Linehold, a brutal, 3CatSpam-friendly grenade launcher backed by a damage-reflecting shield. Whatever Sower’s digging for in L-52, Ironside’s job is simple—make sure no one gets close.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/fac201bd5eed6855fad9f86ac5e444bab86dcdfb.png"]




If you think that’s it—think again. Mesmer didn’t waste time after arriving at L-52. Somehow, he managed to bring Perimeter-9 to his side.


If mercs, headhunters, and private armies had a boogeyman, they’d call it Perimeter-9. Officially labeled a squad of nine mercenaries—but they serve no flag, follow no orders, and chase a goal known only to themselves. Chaotic. Unpredictable. Absolutely merciless. Born and bred in L-52—if such concepts even apply to them.


They were the result of a canceled military experiment: Project P9 (Phantasm). The idea was direct—create a squad of supersoldiers, loyal as tools and deadly as a grenade with the pin pulled. They were meant for deep deployment across timelines, with orders to carry out operations no one else could even survive. As usual, the funding dried up. The experiment needed pharma experts; high command got stingy. You can guess the rest.


The nine subjects—written off, marked for liquidation—turned the tables. They vanished into the deep forest of \[classified], dragging their experimental gear and tactical enhancements with them. Now they operate off the grid—unshackled, undirected, and armed with tech no one can trace. Whatever they were meant to be, they’ve become Perimeter-9 instead.



Callsign "Bratfox”—the most notorious in the unit. Handles diversion, demolition, and solo neutralization of superior enemy elements. 

Shattermark—Bratfox’s personal sniper rifle. Built for brutal efficiency. Features X-ray optics and gadget suppression. Some say victims eliminated by this rifle detonate—but that’s just a story, right?

Silent Fang—a standard sidearm for Perimeter-9. Blinds targets, blocks jumps, and comes with an unsettling edge—Instant Reload. After five hits, the gun seems to reload itself. Nobody’s sure how. 

Tricky Maple—shaped like a maple leaf. Functions like a cluster grenade—with a hint of target-seeking behavior.

Time Forester—the only face in L-52 you might consider a friend. If you're lucky. No one knows who's under the camouflage, but they've called this zone home for decades. At least. Stay on their side. Otherwise, Mesmer won’t be your biggest problem.

Root Piercer—a semi-auto carbine with piercing rounds, blind, and curse effects. High control, tight rhythm—only six shots per reload. Demands precision. Perfect for isolating targets and shutting them down, one cursed bullet at a time.

notes.title: Update
notes.notes:
Claim your place in the Golden Sands. Forge new power—before time runs out.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/b222b41cecba6608a7421743cdf20c429bb20546.png

Pixel Man, Daisy, Human Rebel, and their fellow pixelgunners managed to bring the system back on its feet after the Crash—an attack orchestrated by none other than Eddy Mesmer. But the damage ran deeper than they expected. While patching up the Creator’s PC, the squad discovered something far more alarming: a rift leading to another world.

And not just any world—the Golden Sands. A mysterious realm where the Hourglass Watcher resides, guarding the flow of time and protecting the timelines of the entire Pixel Universe.

But Eddy had already left his mark. The master hypnotist got there first and corrupted Ramlisa, Queen of the Sands and Matriarch of the Ard Al-Mazahib kingdom. Under his control, the once-noble sovereign now leads her forces in a war against the Hourglass Keeper.

What a cruel twist of fate! Pixel Man, Daisy, and Human Rebel have entered the realm of time itself—and time is the one thing they don’t have. If they fail, the Hourglass will shatter, Time’s heartbeat will cease, and all worlds will fall into eternal stillness.

Fortunately, they’re not alone. Reinforcements are on the way—and the sands are far from silent.


 Sands Hunter Khamsin. A silent tracker born of the dunes. He hunts with ancient instincts and answers only to the desert winds.
 Azhar the Djinn. Once bound to forgotten ruins, Azhar now channels timeless power as a proud member of the pixel squad. Also fun fact: he’s our first avatar without feet!
 Sandbite. A Special-class weapon that fuses the mystic essence of timeless sand with modern firepower. It launches explosive orbs of sand dust that blind and slow enemies. The scorpion form is a sanam mutaharrik—a kind of clay-forged golem. No animals are harmed in the process, promise.
 Desert's Judgement. At first glance, it looks like a saif—but don’t be fooled. This is a fully automatic rifle. Instead of bullets, it fires compressed grains of timeless sand. It needs reloading, sure—but you’re never truly out of ammo.
 Golden Wishblade. A rare, elite version of the Desert’s Judgement—crafted exclusively for the arbab al-amwal, the wealthiest citizens of the Ard Al-Mazahib kingdom.
 Little Raakib. An exceptionally well-trained fennec fox who rides a Damun—a massive, flesh-eating sand worm endemic to the harsh dunes of Ard Al-Mazahib. Cute? Definitely. Dangerous? Absolutely.



{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/3c674444493f4ed1bcd806934685da359c10c201.png

In this update’s Set and Lottery, you’ll get a closer look at the many sides of the Chrono-Conflict.


 Queen Ramlisa. Fair, decisive, and radiantly beautiful, Ramlisa once ruled the Ard Al-Mazahib kingdom with grace and wisdom. But even the strongest minds aren’t immune to manipulation—Eddy Mesmer’s hypnotic interference has clouded her judgment, pushing her into a war not her own.
 Gilded Gaze. A royal sidearm that fires charming, ricocheting laser beams wrapped in violet light. 3CatSpammers—take note.
 Hourglass Watcher. No one knows their name. No one knows where they came from. But one thing is certain: without the Watcher’s sacred duty, Time—and the Pixel Universe—would cease to exist.
 Woundweaver. At first glance, just a long wind-scarf adorned with traditional Ard Al-Mazahib patterns. On second glance—a ruthless melee weapon, capable of bleeding out multiple enemies in seconds.
 Desert Verdict. As merciless as the desert itself. This sniper rifle converts timeless sand into searing laser beams, with a high rate of fire to pin down enemies at range. And if someone gets too close, the reload triggers a secret (and painful) close-range defense mechanism.
 Grimoire of Ruin. The most sacred—and feared—book of the Golden Sands. Legend says it was written by a daughter of the sandcaller tribe’s last elder, shortly before her tragic demise. The tribe was wiped out decades ago—falsely accused of treason. But the grimoire survived, carrying within it the power to summon the rage of timeless sand. 3CatSpammers—yes, take another note.

Third time’s a charm! Nani? You bet! Anime Season Vol. 3 is here!

A fresh wave of anime crashes into the Pixel Universe like a divine wind! Don’t even bother bracing yourself—you’re getting blown away no matter what! Let’s see who (and what) is coming:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/35c8ed7766ea5ced6b09bfcda8af41b5c95d1c0e.png

Daisy buys a mysterious box and accidentally opens a portal to a parallel world of Hua-Yun, where elemental spirits grant their power to chosen warriors. But there’s a catch: an ancient spirit named Heiyue has awakened, seeking to consume the moonlight and plunge the world into eternal night. Guess who’s gotta step up, close this Pandora’s box, and save the day (well, technically, a parallel one)?
The good news is that the Hua-Yun kingdom already has a small but determined resistance. And, of course, their own arsenal of unique weapons. Let’s take a closer look at what they’re packing in the parallel dimension.

Fiery and impulsive, as any descendant of dragons, Yang Hua favors the Flaming Lotus assault rifle, equipped with the SuperBurning attribute. Despite his temperament, he’s equally skilled with the Tian Deng sniper rifle. While it doesn’t boast the highest damage, it more than makes up for it with mobility, rapid fire, and effects like X-Ray Vision, Barrier, and Ricochet.
On the other hand, the calm and composed Shui Ling relies on his trusted Hua Hua Rifle, a custom modification of the Tian Deng rifle designed just for him.



{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/9c3f1bcef7640c40ad043826cbf884e928914a99.png

What’s happening on the other side of the conflict? The sinister spirit Heiyue has a dark plan: to consume the moonlight and plunge Hua-Yun into eternal night.

And she has everything she needs to make it happen:

Waning Moon — a laser pistol that charms enemies and grants invisibility to its wielder.
Eclipse Harbinger — a powerful crossbow that blinds with its sheer might.
Moon Phaser — a mystical rocket launcher fueled by the radiant energy of moonlight.

By Heiyue’s side is her loyal companion, the Moon Sentinel. Armed with the Moon Crescent Whisper, a pair of fearsome scythes, he’s the nightmare of Hua-Yun. They say these weapons are used to frighten unruly children—and even careless warriors. 



{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/f0f59767e9ffd48b9d0107d587bfed766a337168.png

How do you take on such powerful enemies, the embodiment of absolute evil? Let the moon guide your path!

Battle other pixelgunners in matches and collect Lunar Stones. Of course, victories will earn you more than just participation. These stones will lead you to rewards reserved for the most elite warriors of Hua-Yun.



{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/12c6d86baaca76754efb76b8f1047566d0149afe.png

Here’s how it works: score frags in battles and trade them for dice rolls. The better your skills, the more rolls you’ll get—and the greater your chances of earning awesome prizes.

The grand prize every pixelgunner should be chasing is the Pixel Games heavy weapon, firing rockets with random effects.

While Pixelman was busy searching for a way out of the Backrooms, things in his hometown of San Blockcisco took a dramatic turn.

For years, the FROST system, run by advanced AI, kept the city’s weather and seasons in perfect balance. But when the CEO of the FROST Corporation devised a sinister plan to take over the system, the entire city fell under their icy control.

Now, San Blockcisco is trapped in eternal winter. The people toil under the corporation’s rule, and Christmas is just a distant memory. The city’s only hope lies with the hacker duo IC3BR3AK3RS—Eliot the MAD and Ellie. Armed with sharp technical skills and custom-built weapons, they’re ready to fight back, whether online or on the frost-covered streets of their beloved city.

The most anomaly-packed season hits PG3D with Update 24.9!


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/37dafcf3216f81eb9e675bcef6ec1ca3efdb48ac.png

The fan-favorite PGA season returns, bringing chills and thrills! Expect eerie new weapons inspired by the strangest SCP Foundation anomalies, plus a special Pixel Pass treat—the Teleporting Relic gadget that completely redefines mobility on the battlefield. Finally, Update 24.9 will conclude the major storyline arc surrounding the search for Pixel Man.

Lore

It turns out those surreal fungal dreams were just a simulated simulation. Daisy awakens in the lab of the PGA—a special agency dedicated to capturing, containing, and destroying dangerous anomalies. The agents know Pixel Man is trapped in the dark depths of the Backrooms, and they’re ready to arm Daisy with whatever it takes to break him free. But there’s a trick to this treat: Daisy must help PGA face the most dangerous anomalies in the Backrooms, threats that could haunt not only San Blockcisco but the entire planet.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/91c3dc4b0f571cefa73f2f6daa115c8bf769fcc8.png

While Daisy battles deadly entities, Pixel Man faces a personal adventure. Trapped in a haunted mansion, he finds himself in endless, gloomy hallways—as if the entire house is nothing but dark, winding corridors.

Help Pixel Man escape from this cursed estate alive! Your task is to choose one of the eerie hallways and follow it to the end for the ultimate reward. At the exit awaits the Halloween avatar Soulskeeper Pumpkin, the spectral laser sniper rifle Soul Angler, and the new Souls Lamp cape.

Only the boldest pixelgunners will brave every gloomy corridor and claim extra rewards. A booster will be your only shield in this ghost-ridden mansion—but the main rewards are within reach for everyone. Will you dare to explore?

The most successful defenders will earn a reward from the mayor—a new weapon, the Anomaly Compass automatic rifle, equipped with a locator to track down enemies.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/04b178f17ec2532baf10d0dff4a7bf7034a18fc3.png

In the new update, you will visit a mysterious forest filled with glowing mushrooms, strange creatures, and, of course, the most dreamlike weapons. You will find the new guns, inspired by fluorescent fungi and insects, hence chitin elements and poisonous attributes. And finally, with Daisy and Black Dragon by your side, you’ll take the next step in the search for Pixel Man story arc.

Lore

After their exhausting journey through Mictlan, Daisy and the Black Dragon find themselves in a mysterious fungi forest. Daisy merely touched an unfamiliar mushroom—it was glowing too brightly to resist. But that one touch was enough to stir the entire forest. Everything around them shimmered with a strange ripple and pulsed in a unified rhythm.

For Daisy and the Black Dragon, that rhythm meant only one thing—the beginning of another adventure. One they would certainly return from, equipped with never-before-seen weapons.

The local beetles can be crafted into a poisonous Beetles Wand. The glowing mushrooms, able to shine through walls, are perfect for small-caliber weapons. The Hypno Frog’s ability to shift gravitational fields turns it into a deadly gadget, while the Dandelion’s explosive seeds transform the flower into compact artillery.

But that’s all in theory. The most interesting things happen in practice, and the mysterious mushroom forest is the ideal testing ground!



{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/d4baecf3322b6de6e7518b893bab07ab9e076422.png

The story-driven Intriguing Wandering grand activity reaches its finale with the third and last chapter: Mysterious Shining. You’ll find out how the adventures of Bubble Queen, Human Rebel, and other pixelgunners ended. Of course, your efforts will be rewarded with unique prizes: the new Berry-Ball gadget, the special Petal Pyro gun, and a skin that completely changes its attributes.

Lore

The pixelgunners defeated Ash Lord and his fiery minions. The Tree of Life was saved, and the raging forest fires were finally extinguished. Yet, even these heroic efforts weren’t enough: thick smoke from the charred remains covered the sky, shrouding the world in an impenetrable fog that blocked out the sun. Only the light of the Shining Flowers can cut through the haze and restore the pixel planet.

notes.title: Update 24.6
Patch Note 24.6
notes.notes:
Let's turn up the heat this summer with a road trip back to the 2000s, a new reporting system, weapons designed by our most talented pixelgunners, and so much more! Ready to roll?

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/c90e85829fa4d7611fc00ea013b74724ade823ca.png

In the wake of the epic showdown, the situation was finally looking up. Portalius, the mad genius, was defeated, and the unpredictable Eddie Mesmer had pulled back – at least for now.

But one problem remained: Pixelman was still lost in the eerie depths of the Backrooms. Time was running out. The longer he stayed trapped, the slimmer the chances of rescue. With no room for error, Daisy and the Black Dragon harnessed Portalius' tech and the Multiverse shards to build a portable Portal Hub. This high-tech device could theoretically jump through time, space, and the unknown fabrics of the Multiverse itself.

But here's the twist: Portalius' reputation as a genius wasn't for nothing. Building a working device from his plans was a beast of a challenge. Daisy messed up the settings, and instead of landing in the Backrooms, she and the Black Dragon found themselves in the early 2000s – inside someone's computer!

The mission? Still the same: fix the Hub and get to the Backrooms. But first, Daisy and her companion had to break out of this retro digital world, where characters from old video games, movies, and anime ran the show. And not all of them were happy to see intruders!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/22942a516b930a6a9ca0835d31cedb945fa259f0.png

In April, we launched the "Your Weapon in the Game'' contest. Despite the name, pixelgunners could submit their creations in any form: weapons, avatars, gadgets, gliders, trails, and more. The grand prize was having their dream concept come true within the game.

In our new event, we imagined what a pixelgunner's workshop might look like. As part of the "Project Task," you'll need to gather parts to create the event's main rewards – guns, an avatar, and a glider. These are the items designed by our players in the contest.

You can collect parts in battles within the marked game modes on designated maps, as well as through purchases in the in-game store. Don’t miss the chance to enhance your Armory with these unique items!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/2b6244af62d0a4549fe2788f60db6ad070ca2f82.png

As part of our fight against cheaters, we've reworked the reporting system. Now you can report dishonest players with just a few clicks, without even quitting the match. Simply select the reason from a list during the kill cam window or from the player table before or after the match, and our support team will receive your report immediately. Each player can send up to 10 reports per day.

This means cheaters will be identified and banned more quickly, as they will be flagged for our anti-cheat system. And what is more, your reports will play a crucial role in improving and tailoring our anti-cheat measures. We’re working together to make our favorite shooter safe and fair for everyone.

This is just one of many upcoming tools of our anti-cheat system, and we will keep you informed about further steps and improvements, so keep an eye out for our social media to be the first ones to know.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/ba4240d8361ab804ec8e9036cc4cd601f0f8a98a.png

PC Edition players, get ready for some crisp new Steam achievements!

For seasoned pixelgunners, hitting 100% completion will be a breeze, and nothing beats that ever-satisfying sound and a pop-up message when you unlock an achievement.

For newcomers, though, it's a different story. Those picking up the Pixel Gun for the first time and chasing achievements have a long and curvy road ahead.

Ultimately, this journey will help rookies have a hand in shooting, explore various game modes, and master the nuances of different weapon categories.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/0e8e7be6ee172c6fc8e6b2aa2b6960faa3bb3a69.png

Clan Refinements

We have some notable changes lined up for clan players in update 24.6 to improve this aspect of the game.

We’ve upgraded the Clan War registration process. Previously, only the clan leader and the officers had access to the Clan War registration. Now, this option is available to every member by default, although it can be disabled in the clan settings.

Secondly, we've reworked the search system, so finding a clan now should be as easy as it gets. To simplify things even more, you can automatically join a clan that meets your criteria with just a click.

Tournament Mode Tweaks

Tournament mode has also received some updates. Based on your feedback, we've adjusted the reward balance, expanded the number of prize spots on the leaderboard, and improved the interface. Soon, we plan to limit the roster of weapons available for the Tournament.

Event Center Enhancements

We've refined the animations, notifications, and icons within the Event Center to make it easier to access information about each game activity (Events, Sets, Lucky Board). No more double-tapping to get straight to the Event. The Lottery icon has come back in the Lobby, so you no longer need to enter the Event Center to get a weapon from a chest, though this option is still available.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44453777/8d60d6d60ec5e182acd2410126cf03d90307aeb4.png

notes.title: Post-Release News and Q&A #1
notes.notes:
That’s just a jaw-dropper! Thank you, pixelgunners, for making this release happen! The party you threw will eternize this moment of pixel glory (our servers will definitely not forget it). In the past day, we achieved incredible results: 25,000 online on Steam – that's top-50 online across the entire platform. We did all this together: each of you contributed to this great success. New challenges and new heights to conquer await us ahead.

Special thanks for your detailed feedback. We see all your messages and are already working on key improvements:


 Logging into the game and getting into the match problems – this is our top priority. Of course, we knew that you wanted the PC Edition bad, but we didn't expect THAT BAD!
 Adjusting the volume of sound effects – we received many requests about this on the release day. Also one of the first candidates for fixing.
 The possibility to turn off sound in the game on the server queue screen – already working on it.
 Gamepad recognition on handheld consoles – every pixelgunner deserves to play the way they find comfortable.
 Key mapping for keyboards and controllers – the second most popular request. Very soon, you will have the opportunity to assign keys at your discretion.
 Moving during viewing the Scoreboard – a small but annoying bug. We're fixing it on the double.
 Locking the Scoreboard on gamepads – adding players to your friendlist is physically inconvenient right now. And friendship is magic, so we're fixing it urgently.
 Graphics settings – the main section in any PC shooter. Very soon, we will add the option to disable motion blur and bloom in the Settings menu.

All these improvements will gradually appear in game patches. Patches will be released regularly, and you can read about all the changes in the News in the Community Hub on Steam or on our Discord.
 
These are our short time plans. What can you expect in the future? Well, for instance, you will definitely get Steam achievements, stickers, cards, and badges, a full support checkmark for Steam Deck, as well as adding friends and inviting them to the game using your Friendlist on Steam.

We also noticed that you are not quite familiar with our Help Center: questions about account transfer topped the support chart. In this regard, we have prepared a small Q&A on the most popular questions. 

You can find a detailed guide on account transfer in a separate news article on Steam or in our Help Center.

On behalf of the entire PG3D team, thanks again to all of you for the support, fun, frags, memorable moments, in a word, for everything! We couldn't have done it without you!

notes.title: Pixel Gun 3D: PC Edition News Update
notes.notes:
Whoa! Your loud reaction to the news about the PG3D PC version exceeded all our expectations. Well, that motivates us to work even harder on the port.

What do you need to know about the Steam version right now?

First, a separate team is working on the port. This way, we maintain mobile version support without being distracted by other developments.

Secondly, PG3D: PC Edition will be almost a complete port of the mobile version. Why almost? We will remove 3-5% of content that became obsolete a long time ago. It will help us speed up the PC version development and also have a positive effect on optimization. Other than that, it will be the same Pixel Gun 3D that you love so much.

Of course, there is more news we have prepared for you. Surely, you are interested in whether it will be possible to transfer progress from the mobile version to the PC. The answer to this and other questions you can get here - on our Steam page. So add PG3D to your wishlist, subscribe to the Steam community and be one of the first to get the news!
